title: Silhouette Scores for Defined Groups in Gene Expression Data
author: Zhao, Sun, et al.

steps.title: Gather microarray CEL files
steps.instruction: Obtain the Affymetrix Rat Genome 230 2.0 Array CEL files for the two datasets: Nakai (31,099 probesets × 24 samples = 3 tissues × 2 conditions × 4 biological replicates) and Kamei (31,099 genes × 10 samples = 5 biological replicates per group).

steps.title: Quantify expression with three algorithms
steps.instruction: Using the affy package in R, quantify probe‑level data with MAS, RMA, and RobLoxBioC algorithms; note that microarray signals are continuous and are typically log‑transformed.

steps.title: Run differential expression analysis
steps.instruction: Apply the limma pipeline (Bioconductor) to each quantified dataset to perform differential expression (DE) analysis; do not use the RNA‑seq TCC pipeline.

steps.title: Perform hierarchical clustering
steps.instruction: Generate hierarchical clustering (HSC) dendrograms for each quantification method (MAS, RMA, RobLoxBioC) using all 31,099 genes; verify three major clusters corresponding to BAT, WAT, and LIV tissues.

steps.title: Set up two‑group comparisons
steps.instruction: Create 15 pairwise group comparisons, each with four biological replicates per group (A1‑A4 vs B1‑B4).

steps.title: Calculate PDEG and AS values
steps.instruction: For each comparison compute the percentage of differentially expressed genes (PDEG) and the average silhouette coefficient (AS).

substeps.instruction: MAS‑quantified data: BAT vs WAT PDEG 24.49–34.98 %; BAT vs LIV PDEG 41.79–44.63 %; WAT vs LIV PDEG 39.74–44.05 %; fed vs fasted PDEG 4.5–8.79 %; intra‑BAT (fed vs fasted) PDEG 8.79 % and AS 0.207.
RobLoxBioC‑quantified data: report similar PDEG/AS trends as MAS.
RMA‑quantified data: observe higher PDEG and AS values than MAS/RobLoxBioC.

steps.title: Analyze Kamei iron‑deficiency dataset
steps.instruction: Compare liver expression between low‑iron diet (≈3 ppm iron for 3 days) and control diet (48 ppm iron). Record that PDEG and AS are close to zero and the HSC dendrogram shows an intermingled structure.

steps.title: Identify outlier samples
steps.instruction: Examine dendrograms for outliers: Iron_def1 is an outlier only in the RMA dendrogram; Iron_def3 is the most distant in MAS and RobLoxBioC dendrograms.

substeps.instruction: Average pairwise distances: RMA 0.007, MAS 0.043, RobLoxBioC 0.037.
Average distances among Kamei liver samples: lower than Nakai liver samples (MAS 0.078, RMA 0.022, RobLoxBioC 0.070).

steps.title: Merge datasets and re‑cluster
steps.instruction: Combine Nakai and Kamei expression matrices (same platform) and generate merged HSC dendrograms; note that the ten Kamei liver samples form a tight cluster that remains tight when eight Nakai liver samples are added.

steps.title: Define distance metric
steps.instruction: Use distance = (1 – Spearman’s r); this metric ranges from 0 to 2 and facilitates interpretation of sample similarity.

steps.title: Record software environment
steps.instruction: Perform all analyses in R version 3.3.2 with Bioconductor packages: TCC 1.14.0, edgeR 3.16.5, ROC 1.50.0, cluster 2.0.5, affy 1.44.0, RobLoxBioC 0.9. R scripts are provided in Additional file 10.
